title: kith-jmap: Session object for /.well-known/jmap
description:
Session object handler: GET /.well-known/jmap returns RFC 8620 §2 Session JSON.

What: Implement an axum GET handler that builds and returns the JMAP Session object with all RFC 8620-required fields, populating role from the caller's verified identity.

Algorithm:
1. Define struct Session and all nested structs (Capabilities, Account, AccountCapabilities) with serde Serialize
2. Handler signature: pub async fn session_handler(caller: Caller, State(state): State<AppState<LocalApiClient>>) -> Json<Session>
3. Build Session:
   a. capabilities.urn:ietf:params:jmap:core = { maxSizeUpload: 104857600, maxConcurrentUpload: 4, maxSizeRequest: 10485760, maxConcurrentRequests: 4, maxCallsInRequest: 16, maxObjectsInGet: 500, maxObjectsInSet: 500, collationAlgorithms: ['i;unicode-casemap'] }
   b. capabilities.urn:kith:chat:1 = { maxBodyBytes: 65536, maxAttachmentBytes: 104857600, supportedBodyTypes: ['text/plain', 'text/markdown'] }
   c. accounts.a-self.name = caller.identity.display() (never empty — Identity::display() guarantees fallback)
   d. accounts.a-self.isPersonal = true, isReadOnly = false
   e. accounts.a-self.accountCapabilities.urn:kith:chat:1.role = match caller.role { Role::Owner => 'owner', Role::Peer => 'peer' }
   f. primaryAccounts.urn:kith:chat:1 = 'a-self'
   g. username = caller.identity.display()
   h. apiUrl, uploadUrl, downloadUrl, eventSourceUrl: construct from base URL (hardcoded or from config)
   i. state = TODO session state token from store (use '0' stub initially, wired later)
4. Return Json(session)

Defensive programming rules:
- All string fields must be non-empty; use Identity::display() which guarantees non-empty
- Capability limit values are hardcoded constants (no user input involved)
- Role comes from verified Caller extractor, never from request body
- URLs are hardcoded templates, not constructed from user input

Tests:
- Owner caller → role = 'owner' in accountCapabilities
- Peer caller → role = 'peer' in accountCapabilities
- Response has all required RFC 8620 §2 fields (capabilities, accounts, primaryAccounts, username, apiUrl, uploadUrl, downloadUrl, eventSourceUrl)
- username is never empty even if identity has empty display_name
Oracle: RFC 8620 §2 field list and required field inventory, not derived from handler code.
